title: "Parameter"
description: "A value learned from data during model training, such as a neural network's weight or bias."
term: "Parameter"

difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

A parameter is a value inside a model that training adjusts. Like a set of
knobs, parameters control how inputs are transformed into predictions.

## Technical explanation

In a parameterized model $f_\theta$, the parameter collection $\theta$
contains learned values. For a neural network, these commonly include weight
matrices and bias vectors. Training updates parameters to reduce an objective
using an optimization algorithm.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Parameter count affects model capacity, memory requirements, communication
cost, and inference speed. Engineers need to distinguish trainable
parameters from fixed settings when estimating resources or selecting a
fine-tuning method.

## How it works

The model uses its current parameters to compute an output and loss.
Backpropagation obtains gradients of the loss with respect to the parameters;
an optimizer then updates them, for example
$\theta \leftarrow \theta-\eta\nabla_\theta L$.

## Practical example

A linear classifier computes scores using a weight matrix and bias. Training
changes those two parameter tensors so that examples of each class receive
more appropriate scores.

## Common misconceptions

- Parameters are learned from training; hyperparameters such as learning
  rate are choices set by the engineer.
- A larger parameter count alone does not determine model quality or
  capability.
